vulnerability.name: GHSA-3f6p-5ww8-9rcr
vulnerability.description: mysql2: auth plugin downgrade to mysql_clear_password leaks plaintext credentials

statements.impact_statement: mysql2 is a MySQL driver the Prisma CLI declares as a dependency for every database it supports; it sits in the image only because `prisma migrate deploy` ships there. This service connects to PostgreSQL exclusively (`prisma.config.ts`, `@prisma/adapter-pg`), so no MySQL handshake, and therefore no auth plugin negotiation, ever runs. Prisma pins the exact version, so it moves when Prisma does.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-40345
vulnerability.description: deepmerge-ts: stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs

statements.impact_statement: The only consumer in the image is `@prisma/config`, which merges the defaults of the Prisma CLI with the operator's own `prisma.config.ts` when `migrate deploy` starts. Both inputs are authored by the operator and shipped inside the image; no external party can supply an object to that merge. The server bundle carries its own, fixed copy (8.x) for html-to-text. Prisma pins the exact version, so it moves when Prisma does.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-75804
vulnerability.description: OpenSSL: denial of service via unenforced QUIC connection flow control

statements.impact_statement: Neither the server nor the migration tooling uses QUIC or DTLS. Node carries its own statically linked OpenSSL and never loads the system library (`node_shared_openssl` is false, no `libssl` in its dynamic dependencies). The only consumer of the system `libssl3t64` is Prisma's `schema-engine` binary, run by `migrate deploy`, which opens a TLS-over-TCP client connection to PostgreSQL: it imports `TLS_method` and the `SSL_*` client calls, and no QUIC or DTLS function at all. Scoped to this exact version: the statement stops matching once the distroless base image ships Debian's fix (`3.5.7-1~deb13u3`), which had not happened when it was written.
